literal: Ancestors, gods, guests, relatives, oneself, saying thus, to cherish these five ways is the foremost duty.
translation: To cherish the fivefold duties toward ancestors, gods, guests, relatives, and oneself is the householder's foremost duty.
modern: தென்புலத்தார் (முன்னோர்), தெய்வம், விருந்தினர், சுற்றத்தார், தான் ஆகிய ஐந்து இடங்களிலும் செய்ய வேண்டிய கடமைகளைப் போற்றிச் செய்தல் இல்லறத்தானுக்கு முதன்மையான கடமையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the five essential duties of a householder. The five categories are tenpulattār (ancestors), teyvam (gods), viruntu (guests), okkal (relatives), and tāṉ (oneself). The word ōmpal means to cherish or protect, indicating that these are active duties of support. The poet concludes that fulfilling these five obligations is the talai (foremost or supreme) duty of domestic life.
